goals: MECHANISTIC (feasible subset): estimate spatial variation in deep drainage / recharge flux across the basin as a function of soil texture and land-use proxy
TRANSPORT (requested target, INFEASIBLE): move fertilizer-derived nitrate from fields to well screens and estimate arrival concentration
VALIDATION (requested, INFEASIBLE): compare modeled nitrate against well nitrate records
key_processes: surface/subsurface water partitioning and recharge (ELM, feasible)
soil N leaching below root zone (not a usable output)
lateral saturated-zone advection/dispersion of nitrate (no capability)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column can produce recharge/deep-drainage flux under different soil and land-use-proxy treatments — the only link in the requested nitrate chain this stack can represent. It cannot generate a nitrate solute, transport it laterally, or predict well concentrations.
model_choice.coupling_note: Answering the actual question requires ELM->reactive-transport coupling (recharge AND a nitrate mass flux -> a solute transport model). Neither the nitrate flux, the reactive-transport model, nor the coupler exists; listed under requires_capabilities.

answerable: Spatial variation in recharge / deep-drainage flux (QDRAI/QRECHARGE) across soil and land-use-proxy strata
Soil-texture control on water partitioning (ET vs runoff vs drainage) within the basin

not_answerable.aspect: Nitrate arrival concentration at drinking-water wells
not_answerable.why: ELM does not output a transportable nitrate solute flux; single-column ELM has no lateral groundwater transport; PFLOTRAN as available is steady-state flow only (no reactive solute transport); no ELM->transport coupler exists.
not_answerable.needs: reactive nitrate transport model + nitrogen leaching flux output + ELM->transport coupling

not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral or regional groundwater flow; no routing.
not_answerable.needs: lateral/regional groundwater flow model + flow-path travel-time capability

not_answerable.why: There is no modeled nitrate quantity to compare against the observations.
not_answerable.needs: modeled nitrate concentration output (dependent on the above)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: Low relief (~160 m) makes NLDAS forcing near-uniform, so soil x land-use is the only representable lever. 3 soil classes x 2 land-use proxies = 6 columns spans the recharge-relevant heterogeneity without a blind grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate on fertilized row-crop uplands (the nominal nitrate source) over contrasting SSURGO drainage classes, since recharge magnitude — the one deliverable — is dominated by soil drainage; include background non-fertilized analogs for contrast.
sampling_strategy.replication: None — each stratum is a single characterizing column; the study is scoping recharge magnitudes, not statistical inference.

sampling_plan.reason: Highest-recharge source setting — upper bound on downward water (and thus potential nitrate leaching) flux from fertilized fields.
Typical basin condition — central estimate of recharge beneath fertilized fields.
Low-recharge / high-runoff source setting — where drainage-tile vs surface loss partitioning matters most.
Recharge baseline for a coarse soil absent the row-crop land-use proxy.
Recharge baseline for the dominant loam under non-cropped cover.
Recharge baseline for poorly-drained soil to bound land-use vs soil effects on drainage.

validation_design.comparison: NONE POSSIBLE — the stack produces no modeled nitrate concentration to compare against; observations cannot be used as posed
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — moot until nitrate transport is modeled

validation_design.comparison: qualitative sanity check against literature recharge ranges for Iowa row-crop settings (analog, not co-located)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS forcing, native SSURGO soil per stratum, with spin-up (recharge is a slow state and requires warm-start/spin-up)

requires_capabilities.capability: nitrogen leaching / nitrate mass flux output from ELM
requires_capabilities.why: no transportable nitrate quantity is produced
requires_capabilities.blocks: any estimate of nitrate leaving fields

requires_capabilities.why: PFLOTRAN as available is steady-state flow only
requires_capabilities.blocks: transport of nitrate from field to well

requires_capabilities.capability: lateral / regional groundwater flow + flow-path travel time
requires_capabilities.why: single-column ELM has no lateral transport

requires_capabilities.capability: ELM -> transport-model coupling (recharge + nitrate flux as BC)

requires_capabilities.why: needed to validate the modeled concentrations once they exist
recharge is a slow state; cold-start columns read ~0 recharge while storage fills
requires_capabilities.blocks: credible recharge magnitudes even for the feasible subset

requires_capabilities.why: the land-use driver must be mapped to columns

assumptions: Land-use classes are treated as a surface/soil-management proxy; the framework has no fertilizer application module.
Basin relief (~160 m) is too small for NLDAS to produce meaningful orographic forcing contrast, so soil is the dominant lever for recharge.
SSURGO soil classes can be resolved at chosen column locations.
open_questions: Is the actual deliverable acceptable as 'recharge beneath fertilized fields' (feasible), or is the nitrate concentration at wells non-negotiable (infeasible with current stack)?
Are there measured recharge or drainage-tile flux data in-domain to validate the recharge subset?
Which reactive-transport engine is intended for the nitrate step, and would fertilizer application rates / timing be provided?
